questions.question_text: What is the minimum educational qualification required to apply for the Associate Degree in Economics at FJWU?
questions.explanation: Admission to the Associate Degree program typically requires completion of 12 years of formal education, commonly known as Intermediate or HSSC level.

questions.question_text: Which stream of study at the Intermediate level is typically preferred for candidates seeking admission to the Associate Degree in Economics?
questions.explanation: While open to various streams, students with a background in Commerce, Economics, or Mathematics are generally better prepared for the core curriculum of an Economics degree.

questions.question_text: Does Fatima Jinnah Women University require candidates to have a specific minimum percentage in their HSSC for the Associate Degree in Economics?
questions.explanation: Most public sector universities in Pakistan set a minimum merit threshold, which is generally 45% for undergraduate-level admissions.

questions.question_text: What is the policy regarding age limits for applicants to the Associate Degree in Economics at FJWU?
options: No upper age limit for any applicant
Must be under 30 years of age
questions.explanation: FJWU typically does not impose an upper age limit for admission into undergraduate Associate Degree programs.

questions.question_text: Are students who have completed their A-Levels eligible to apply for the Associate Degree in Economics?
options: No, only HSSC students are eligible
Yes, provided they provide an Equivalence Certificate from IBCC
Yes, but they must repeat their O-Levels
No, FJWU only accepts local HSSC boards
questions.explanation: Candidates with A-Levels must submit an official Equivalence Certificate issued by the Inter Board Committee of Chairmen (IBCC) to be considered.

questions.question_text: Is a gap year after HSSC a disqualifying factor for admission to the Associate Degree program?
options: Yes, only fresh graduates are eligible
No, gap years are allowed as long as the applicant meets criteria
Yes, unless they provide a gap justification letter
Only one gap year is permitted
questions.explanation: FJWU accepts applications from students regardless of when they completed their previous studies, provided they meet the minimum percentage requirement.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum HSSC subject requirement, if any, for students from a non-economics background to be considered for the Associate Degree in Economics?
options: Mathematics must be a core subject
Any stream of HSSC (FA/FSc/I.Com) is generally eligible
Only Science stream students are eligible
History must be passed at the HSSC level
questions.explanation: FJWU typically accepts students from diverse academic backgrounds for the Associate Degree, provided they meet the minimum percentage criteria.

questions.question_text: How is the 'Equivalence Certificate' used in the admission of A-Level students?
options: It replaces the need for a secondary school certificate
It validates that the candidate's A-Level grades meet the local HSSC standards
It is only required for international students
It serves as a character reference
questions.explanation: The IBCC Equivalence Certificate is mandatory for A-Level students to ensure their grades are comparable to the Pakistani HSSC system.

questions.question_text: Is there an upper age limit for female candidates applying to the Associate Degree program at FJWU?
options: No specific upper age limit is enforced
questions.explanation: FJWU programs are generally open to applicants who meet the academic qualifications without a restrictive upper age barrier.

questions.question_text: To be eligible for the Associate Degree in Economics at FJWU, what is the minimum required status of a candidate's intermediate result?
questions.explanation: Admission typically requires the candidate to have successfully cleared their Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) or equivalent.

questions.question_text: In addition to HSSC, which academic record is mandatory for internal verification of the student's eligibility?
options: Secondary School Certificate (SSC) or Matric equivalent
questions.explanation: Verification of basic schooling is essential to establish educational continuity and eligibility.
